# `select_dyadic_surface`

the dyadic equal-area tiles of a surface as one grid with closed-form levels, from a stated finest tile (subject, group tree, or transfer onto the group tree).

Version 1, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run select_dyadic_surface --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run select_dyadic_surface --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run select_dyadic_surface --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --surface cortex --rule subject --finest "20 mm"
nxr-neuro run select_dyadic_surface --dataset <folder> --subject @default_subject --surface cortex_pial --rule group --finest "10 mm"
nxr-neuro run select_dyadic_surface --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --surface cortex --rule transfer
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `surface` | manifold surface, where {"name": "$surface"} (name the surface (--surface)) | yes |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `surface` | `--surface` | none | - |  | the surface whose tiles are made, by name |
| `rule` | `--rule` | `subject` | - | subject, group, transfer | subject = the surface's own tiles \| group = the default subject's tiles as the group tree \| transfer = this subject's vertices on the group tree through the registered spheres |
| `finest` | `--finest` | none | mm |  | the finest tile as a quantity: a tile diameter (20 mm), a tile area (area 400 mm2), a wavelength (wavelength 40 mm) or parts per hemisphere (parts 256); the depth is resolved from it; null: the finest every piece reaches; rule transfer takes the template's |
| `resolution` | `--resolution` | `fsaverage5` | - |  | rule group: the template's resolution, recorded in the atlas definitions |
| `atlas_finest` | `--atlas-finest` | none | mm |  | rule group: the finest tile of the dataset's atlases as a quantity (the grid must reach it); null: the grid's finest |
| `frame_rate` | `--frame-rate` | `36 frames/cycle` | frames/cycle |  | rule group: the default frame density recorded in the atlas definitions (frames per cycle of the band's centre; the origin of frames is a parameter of `select_time_grid`) |

## Notes from the definition

```text
THE DYADIC TILES OF A SURFACE: ONE maker (the node `select.dyadic_surface`) for the three ways a surface gets its grid. A grid with closed-form levels (the Studio's `surfaceLadder`, nxr `geom.ladder`, Rheome
`+geom/surfaceladder.m`): each tile halved by equal mass across its geodesic diameter, every tile ONE PIECE; level l has 2^l tiles per connected piece, paired with the band it adds by Weyl's law. The hierarchy is a
closed form (member number >> (D - l)); no parent map is stored. The finest tile is a QUANTITY (a tile diameter in mm, a tile area in mm2, a wavelength in mm or parts per hemisphere), never a level index; the depth D
is resolved from it, and the run records the stated quantity, its chart, the resolved level and the SNAPPED quantity (the level's measured mean tile diameter).

  rule subject   the surface's own tiles (tree subject)
  rule group     the default subject's tiles as the dataset's GROUP TREE, with the atlas definitions (the atlas leaf, the resolution, the default bands, the default trajectory scales)
  rule transfer  the subject's vertices on the group tree through the registered spheres, keeping the template's codes (a tile no vertex reaches is an empty member), stored as `<surface> tiles transfer`
                 beside the subject's own `<surface> tiles`

Per level the stored attributes are {area_m2, diameter_mm, weyl_band_per_m2}. The Levi-Civita connection between neighbouring tiles is NOT part of the grid: it is a measurement over the product of a level with itself,
made by `measure` with the measure `levi_civita` over `select_product`.

What it cannot resolve: a tile is as equal in area as the cut across the geodesic diameter allows; a surface of several pieces gets piece slots and a piece too small for the finest level stops the ladder there.

  nxr-neuro run select_dyadic_surface --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --surface cortex --rule subject --finest "20 mm"
  nxr-neuro run select_dyadic_surface --dataset <folder> --subject @default_subject --surface cortex_pial --rule group --finest "10 mm"
  nxr-neuro run select_dyadic_surface --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --surface cortex --rule transfer
```
